data_output.description: data.encode(splits) remains unchanged and returns (encoded, dimension). encoded["train"] is (train_features, train_labels, train_users), where train_users is aligned one-to-one with training rows and is derived from the exact raw user_id field. encoded["valid"] remains (valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users) in canonical selected source-row order.

model_input.description: Model.step(features, labels, sample_weights=None) accepts features shaped (batch_rows, 7), labels shaped (batch_rows,), and optional finite nonnegative float32-compatible sample_weights shaped (batch_rows,). Trainer supplies globally mean-one normalized inverse training-user-impression-count weights. Model.predict(features) continues to return one raw-logit score per input row in unchanged order.

model_designer.objective: Implement weighted binary cross-entropy support in model.py so the trainer can apply normalized inverse training-user-impression-count weights without changing the FM architecture or optimizer settings.
required_changes: Change Model.step in model.py to accept an optional third argument sample_weights, with the existing two-argument call behavior retained when sample_weights is None.

For a nonempty batch with supplied sample_weights, convert it to a float32 vector, validate that it is one-dimensional, has exactly len(labels) elements, is finite, and has no negative values; raise ValueError on violation.

Compute the per-example logit derivative as (probabilities - labels) * sample_weights / size, where size is the batch length. This implements the requested mean-weight-one weighted BCE while retaining the baseline batch-size gradient normalization.

Return the weighted mean BCE when sample_weights is supplied: mean(sample_weights * (-(labels*log(probabilities+1e-9)+(1-labels)*log(1-probabilities+1e-9)))); retain the exact existing unweighted loss calculation when sample_weights is None.

Apply the same weighted gradient vector to the linear-weight, embedding, and bias updates. Do not alter Adam constants, L2 treatment, initialization, prediction logits, state/load_state behavior, or Model constructor defaults.
preserve: Keep all feature processing outside model.py unchanged.
Keep unweighted Model.step(features, labels) behavior numerically equivalent to the parent implementation.
Keep predict returning raw logits in input row order.
coordination_notes: Trainer will call Model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch], train_weights[batch]). sample_weights is a per-row float32 array already normalized globally across the full training split to arithmetic mean 1.0; Model.step must not renormalize it per batch.
No config.json edit is required for this fixed loss-only ablation; do not add a loss setting or alter configured hyperparameters.

trainer.objective: Implement train-only normalized inverse user-impression-count sample weights in train.py and pass them to the model for every training update, while preserving the fixed evaluator output contract.
required_changes: In train.py, retain the third encoded training output by changing the training unpacking to train_features, train_labels, train_users = encoded["train"].

Immediately after loading encoded training data, derive counts only from train_users: use the exact user_id values emitted by data.encode, count each user's total number of rows in the training split, and construct train_weights as float32 reciprocal counts for each corresponding training row.

Normalize train_weights once over the complete training split by dividing by its arithmetic mean, so float(train_weights.mean()) is 1.0 up to float32 precision. Validate nonempty training data, finite positive weights, and a positive finite mean before normalization; raise ValueError if these conditions are violated.

In the epoch minibatch loop, call model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch], train_weights[batch]) for every batch. Do not reorder train_users independently of the existing seeded permutation.

In --contract-check mode, derive weights from the contract-check training slice using the same complete loaded train split logic, and call model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size], train_weights[:probe_size]) so the weighted-step interface is exercised.
Do not change config.json because all configured model, feature, optimizer, seed, schedule, batch size, patience, and split settings must remain exactly as in the parent experiment.
preserve: Preserve load and encode behavior and use no validation labels, validation user counts, test rows, or non-training rows to derive weights.
Preserve the existing seeded permutation, epoch count, early stopping selection metrics, checkpoint restoration, and all config values.

Preserve the fixed command output: np.savez(args.output, row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels), dtype=np.int64), scores=model.predict(valid_features)). row_ids and scores must have exactly one entry per canonical encoded validation row, in canonical validation row order.
Ground-truth labels remain used only for the existing internal training-selection metrics and are not written into predictions_valid.npz.
coordination_notes: data.py already supplies encoded tuples as (features, labels, users), where users originate from the exact eligible raw user_id column in log_standard_4_08_to_4_21_pure.csv for training. Do not modify data.py and do not introduce a source-column alias.

The canonical weighting recipe is: for every training row i, count_i = number of rows j in encoded train with train_users[j] == train_users[i]; raw_weight_i = 1.0 / count_i; train_weight_i = raw_weight_i / mean(raw_weight over all training rows).
Pass the globally normalized weights unchanged into Model.step; model_designer owns the weighted-BCE gradient and weighted loss implementation.

reasoning: This is a loss-only ablation. The existing data interface already exposes the exact eligible raw user_id values for the training split, so no data.py change is needed. Trainer-owned code must derive the train-only reciprocal-frequency weights and model-owned code must apply them to BCE gradients. Global mean-one normalization preserves the requested overall loss scale while shifting aggregate training mass toward equal user contribution. No config change is needed because the ablation must retain every configured setting unchanged.
